messages:
maria: quick sync — proposing adaptive prebind windows for routing. idea: routers probe a small candidate set and wait a tenant-specific window before committing so cheaper routes can win without blowing latency.
kevin: where does the logic live? router-local sketch or central policy?
maria: router-local. maintain a lightweight t-digest per tenant/route-class; window_ms = clamp(alpha * p95, min, max). default alpha=0.8, min=20, max=300.
tara: be careful with batching. holding slots can block batch formation and hurt throughput.
akshay: +1. for Dedicated we expose a /prebind that returns a single-use token + ttl; runtime best-effort honors it. add TTL short (200-400ms).
olivia: DSL change: allow optional adaptive_window stanza. example: "prefer": {"mode":"cost","adaptive_window":{"q":0.95,"alpha":"0.8","min_ms":"30","max_ms":"200"}}
sam: ops: emit routing.window_ms, probe_count, prebind_held, fallback_rate per tenant. alert if fallback_rate > 5% or window_latency_delta_p95 > 15ms over 5m.
akshay: simulator: add --freeze-windows and a worst-case injection mode to validate safety.
maria: rollout: sample 5% interactive lanes, non-batched only, staging POC, monitor metrics, then widen. action owners: @kevin prebind proto, @olivia DSL PR, @akshay sim flags, @tara batching sim, @sam dashboards.
infra-bot: deploy: staging image router-adaptivewin-2026-03-23 pushed.
maria: noted, will coordinate canary next week.
